related_questions.question: How many times am I going to get COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Reinfection with the virus that causes COVID-19 occurs when you are infected, recover, and then get infected again. You can get reinfected multiple times. Staying up to date on vaccines and seeking treatment for a COVID-19 infection can help decrease the risk of experiencing severe illness.
related_questions.title: About Reinfection | COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: Is long covid increasing or decreasing?
related_questions.snippet: While data are limited, the chance of developing post COVID-19 condition appears to be lower now than earlier in the pandemic. However, the virus is still circulating widely, and every new infection is associated with a risk.
related_questions.title: Post COVID-19 condition (long COVID) - World Health Organization (WHO)

related_questions.question: How serious is catching COVID-19 now?
related_questions.snippet: Many people with COVID-19, also called coronavirus disease 2019, recover at home. But for some, COVID-19 can be a serious illness. Some people may need care in the hospital, treatment in the intensive care unit and the need for breathing help. In some people, severe COVID-19 illness can lead to death.
related_questions.title: COVID-19: Who's at higher risk of serious symptoms? - Mayo Clinic

related_questions.question: Is the COVID pandemic still going on?

text_blocks.snippet: While the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an end to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on May 5, 2023, COVID-19 continues to circulate. The pandemic's official end is not clearly defined, and whether it's still considered a pandemic depends on the definition used. Currently, COVID-19 vaccines continue to offer protection against severe disease and death according to the WHO.
